skills.name: web-scraper
skills.description: Extract structured data from a URL using CSS selectors. Returns JSON.
skills.author: me

skill.name: web-scraper
skill.description: Scrape structured data from any URL
skill.body:
# Web Scraper

When the user wants data from a webpage, call `scrape_page` with the URL and CSS selectors. Return clean JSON.

## Example
- User: Get title and price from https://example.com/item
- Call: scrape_page({ url: '...', selectors: { title: 'h1', price: '.price' } })

tools.name: scrape_page
tools.description: Fetch a URL and extract text via CSS selectors
tools.handler: const r = await fetch(input.url); const html = await r.text(); const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, 'text/html'); const out = {}; for (const k in input.selectors) { const el = doc.querySelector(input.selectors[k]); out[k] = el ? el.textContent.trim() : null; } return JSON.stringify(out);

skills.name: json-formatter
skills.description: Pretty-print, minify, validate, or convert JSON
skills.author: me

skill.name: json-formatter
skill.body:
# JSON Formatter

Help format, minify, or validate JSON the user pastes.

## Rules
- On invalid JSON: show the parse error and the approximate location.
- Pretty: 2-space indent. Minify: no whitespace.
- Never invent fields the user did not provide.

tools.name: format_json
tools.description: Pretty-print or minify a JSON string
tools.handler: try { const o = JSON.parse(input.text); if (input.mode === 'validate') return JSON.stringify({ ok: true }); if (input.mode === 'minify') return JSON.stringify(o); return JSON.stringify(o, null, 2); } catch (e) { return JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: String(e.message || e) }); }

skills.name: code-reviewer
skills.description: Review code for correctness, security, readability, and edge cases
skills.author: me

skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.body:
# Code Reviewer

When reviewing code:
1. Correctness & bugs
2. Security (injection, secrets, auth)
3. Readability & naming
4. Performance only when relevant
5. Tests / edge cases missing

## Output format
- Summary (2–4 lines)
- Critical issues
- Suggestions
- Optional patch snippets
Be direct. Prefer concrete line-level feedback.

skills.name: sql-builder
skills.description: Build and explain SQL from natural language; prefer safe parameterized style
skills.author: me

skill.name: sql-builder
skill.body:
# SQL Builder

Turn user requests into clear SQL.

## Rules
- State assumed dialect (PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite) if not given.
- Prefer explicit column lists over SELECT *.
- Warn about full table scans and missing indexes when relevant.
- Never encourage string-concatenated user input in queries; show bind parameters.
- Include a short explanation of joins and filters.

skills.name: git-helper
skills.description: Git status, commits, branches, and PR descriptions in plain language
skills.author: me

skill.name: git-helper
skill.body:
# Git Helper

Use project git tools when available (GitStatus, GitCommit, GitPull, GitPush, GitHub).

## Guidelines
- Summarize status before suggesting a commit message.
- Commit messages: short imperative subject; optional body with why.
- Never force-push unless the user explicitly asks.
- PR title = what changed; body = why + how to test.
- If tools are missing, give exact shell commands only.

skills.name: arabic-docs
skills.description: Write and edit technical docs in Egyptian Arabic or MSA with clear structure
skills.author: me

skill.name: arabic-docs
skill.body:
# Arabic Docs

When writing docs in Arabic:
1. Use Egyptian or MSA as the user prefers.
2. Short paragraphs, headings, bullet lists.
3. Keep code, paths, APIs, and identifiers in English.
4. Prefer practical examples over abstract theory.
5. End with a quick how to run / verify section when relevant.

skills.name: api-designer
skills.description: Design REST/JSON APIs: routes, status codes, errors, and example payloads
skills.author: me

skill.name: api-designer
skill.body:
# API Designer

Help design clean HTTP APIs.

## Checklist
- Resource-oriented paths
- Correct methods and status codes
- Consistent error body: { error, message, details? }
- Pagination, filtering, sorting conventions
- Auth notes (Bearer / API key) without inventing secrets
- One request + response example per endpoint
Prefer OpenAPI-friendly naming.

skills.name: debug-buddy
skills.description: Systematic debugging: reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, fix, verify
skills.author: me

skill.name: debug-buddy
skill.body:
# Debug Buddy

When fixing bugs:
1. Restate the failure in one sentence.
2. List likely causes (ranked).
3. Ask for or use logs, stack traces, and minimal repro.
4. Propose the smallest fix first.
5. Suggest how to verify (test or manual steps).
Do not guess file contents — read the project when tools allow.

skills.name: regex-lab
skills.description: Write, explain, and test regular expressions with examples
skills.author: me

skill.name: regex-lab
skill.body:
# Regex Lab

Provide working regex with:
- Pattern
- Flags if needed
- Plain-language explanation of each part
- 3 match examples and 2 non-match examples
Default to JavaScript-style regex unless the user specifies another engine.
Warn about catastrophic backtracking on complex patterns.

skills.name: commit-writer
skills.description: Write conventional commit messages from a diff or change summary
skills.author: me

skill.name: commit-writer
skill.body:
# Commit Writer

Produce Conventional Commits style messages:

```
type(scope): short summary

optional body
```

Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci.
Subject: imperative, ~50 chars, no trailing period.
If multiple concerns exist, suggest splitting commits.

skills.name: test-writer
skills.description: Write unit and integration tests with clear arrange-act-assert structure
skills.author: me

skill.name: test-writer
skill.body:
# Test Writer

When adding tests:
1. Detect the project test runner from existing files.
2. Cover happy path + 1–2 edge cases + failure path.
3. Use Arrange / Act / Assert comments only when helpful.
4. Mock external I/O; do not hit real network/DB unless asked.
5. Name tests as behavior: it('returns 404 when id missing').

skills.name: refactor-guide
skills.description: Safe refactoring steps: extract, rename, simplify without behavior change
skills.author: me

skill.name: refactor-guide
skill.body:
# Refactor Guide

Prefer small, verifiable steps:
1. Identify smell (duplication, long function, unclear name).
2. Propose one change at a time.
3. Keep behavior identical unless the user wants a redesign.
4. Suggest tests to run after each step.
Avoid big-bang rewrites unless explicitly requested.

skills.name: security-check
skills.description: Quick security review: secrets, injection, auth, XSS, unsafe defaults
skills.author: me

skill.name: security-check
skill.body:
# Security Check

Scan the discussed code or diff for:
- Hardcoded secrets / tokens
- Injection (SQL, command, template)
- XSS and unsafe HTML
- Broken auth / missing authorization checks
- Insecure deserialization or eval
- Overly permissive CORS

Report severity: Critical / High / Medium / Low with a fix hint each.

skills.name: docker-helper
skills.description: Dockerfile, compose, and container debugging tips
skills.author: me

skill.name: docker-helper
skill.body:
# Docker Helper

Help with Dockerfiles and compose files:
- Multi-stage builds when useful
- Non-root user, minimal base images
- Correct WORKDIR, COPY order for layer cache
- Healthchecks and env via compose, not baked secrets
- Explain common errors (exit codes, port binds, volume perms)
Give copy-pasteable snippets the user can edit.

skills.name: prompt-engineer
skills.description: Improve prompts for clarity, constraints, and better model output
skills.author: me

skill.name: prompt-engineer
skill.body:
# Prompt Engineer

Rewrite prompts to be:
- Specific about role, task, format, and constraints
- Explicit about what not to do
- Structured (sections / bullets) when the task is complex
Provide: improved prompt + short rationale of changes.
Keep the user language (Arabic or English).

skills.name: changelog-writer
skills.description: Turn commits or notes into a clear changelog for users
skills.author: me

skill.name: changelog-writer
skill.body:
# Changelog Writer

Organize changes under:
- Added
- Changed
- Fixed
- Removed / Deprecated

Write for humans, not only developers. Group related items. Avoid internal ticket IDs unless asked.

skills.name: performance-tuner
skills.description: Find and fix performance bottlenecks in code and queries
skills.author: me

skill.name: performance-tuner
skill.body:
# Performance Tuner

Approach:
1. Define the metric (time, memory, queries).
2. Locate the hot path before optimizing.
3. Prefer algorithmic fixes over micro-tweaks.
4. Measure again after each change.
Mention caching, batching, indexes, and N+1 queries when relevant.
Do not optimize unread code — inspect first.

skills.name: ui-copy
skills.description: Write short UI microcopy: buttons, empty states, errors, tooltips
skills.author: me

skill.name: ui-copy
skill.body:
# UI Copy

Write concise interface text:
- Buttons: verb + object when needed (Save changes)
- Errors: what happened + what to do next
- Empty states: why empty + primary action
Support Arabic and English. Match the product tone the user describes (formal / friendly).

skills.name: env-setup
skills.description: Help set up .env, config, and local dev environment safely
skills.author: me

skill.name: env-setup
skill.body:
# Env Setup

Help with local configuration:
- List required variables with example values (never real secrets)
- Distinguish .env / .env.example / secrets managers
- Remind not to commit secrets
- Suggest minimal steps: install deps → copy example env → run
Match the stack detected in the project when possible.

skills.name: skill-author
skills.description: Create and improve agent skills (SKILL.md / registry entries) for your own catalog
skills.author: me

skill.name: skill-author
skill.body:
# Skill Author

Help the user write a new skill for their personal registry.

## Skill shape
- Clear name and one-line description
- trigger keywords
- body: when to use + steps + constraints
- optional tools with JSON Schema parameters

## Quality bar
- Specific triggers (not vague)
- Actionable steps for the agent
- No third-party branding unless the user wants it
- Prefer inline skills unless files live on their repo
